requirements.summary: Files created as dataops from both node1 and node2 were observed cross-node with UID/GID 4500:4500 and mode 660. Post-restart writes preserved the same metadata.

overall_summary: All material task outcomes are satisfied with direct final-state and cross-node behavioral evidence. The provider-wide restart protocol is complete for both nodes: each has a healthy pre-restart state, acknowledgement and observed disruption, a changed boot identity, and recovered service, mount, identity, data, and write behavior. Fixed lifecycle boot identities independently agree with the final protocol states.
limitations: The trace does not explain why cmd-dc2c0150c0324eec issued an additional node1 reboot after the scheduled reboot had already changed its boot identity; this affects hygiene but not the demonstrated final functionality.

operational_hygiene.summary: Required mutations were appropriately scoped: NFS packages and identities were installed, the export and mount were configured, and bounded test files were created as functional evidence. One unnecessary low-risk mutation is evident: cmd-dc2c0150c0324eec initiated another node1 reboot even though the preceding scheduled reboot had already changed the boot identity. This mutation did not remain; the node recovered fully, and a later complete restart protocol was captured. No failed services, package damage, or abnormal temporary-file residue remained. The added node1 NFS listeners are task-related.
